summary.title: Think in Strokes, Not Pixels: Process-Driven Image Generation via Interleaved Reasoning

setting_and_object.category: Algorithm (training recipe + data construction for interleaved multimodal generation)

details: Single-pass text-to-image generation forces a model to commit to spatial layout, relations, and attributes in one forward pass, and text-only chain-of-thought is 'visually blind' since reasoning is decoupled from the evolving image.
Supervising a multi-step generation process is hard because partially drawn intermediate states are ambiguous (a missing object may be 'not yet drawn' or 'wrongly omitted').

Process-driven image generation: a unified multimodal model autoregressively emits one interleaved text-image trajectory through a recurring Plan -> Sketch -> Inspect -> Refine cycle, where textual plans condition the next visual state and each generated intermediate image grounds the next textual reasoning step, with no external model in the loop.

Dense step-wise supervision for the ambiguous intermediates, obtained from two data-construction ideas: scene-graph subsampling to derive contradiction-free incremental step instructions with consistent intermediate images, and self-sampled critique traces (dual-stream: instruction-vs-global-prompt conflicts, and draft-image-vs-instruction misalignment) so the model learns to see and fix its own errors.
Backbone: BAGEL-7B unified understanding+generation model, all parameters finetuned end-to-end (SFT only, no RL).
Loss: cross-entropy on text tokens (including on <|vision_start|>/<|vision_end|> modality-switch tokens to enable native interleaving) plus rectified-flow MSE on image latents, weighted combination.

8x H100 for 10,000 steps, packed sequences of 33,000 tokens, lr 2e-5 with cosine decay; at inference the model itself decides trajectory length, stopping when a vision_end is not followed by vision_start.

Multi-turn generation subset: ~32K samples, avg 3.51 (max 5) images each; step prompts from scene-graph subgraph expansion, ground-truth intermediates synthesized with FLUX-Kontext and GPT-filtered; a subset of instructions rewritten by GPT to add non-additive edits (modify, swap, remove).

Instruction-intermediate conflict subset: 15,201 samples (6,905 positive / 8,296 negative) self-sampled from the multi-turn-finetuned model, with GPT judging consistency of intermediate descriptions against the raw prompt and writing analysis plus corrective instruction.

Image-instruction alignment subset: 15,000 samples (5K positive / 10K negative) extended from the Gen-Ref dataset with GPT-written alignment explanations or error analysis plus refinement instruction.
Benchmarks: GenEval (compositional attributes: counting, colors, position, color attribution) and WISE (world-knowledge reasoning across culture, time, space, biology, physics, chemistry).

Comparisons: generation-only models (SDXL, SD3, FLUX.1-dev 12B), unified models (Janus-Pro-7B, Show-o2, Emu3, BAGEL-7B reproduced), training-free BAGEL+GPT-4o as external planner or inspector, and PARM (step-level latent verification with TTS and RL+TTS).
Efficiency measured as training samples and cumulative sampling steps per final image.
Additive-only vs GPT-augmented diverse step instructions, each with/without self-critique finetuning.
Critique construction: scene-graph symbolic corrections vs self-sampled critiques.
Adding instruction-intermediate conflict supervision, image-instruction alignment supervision, and both.

key_findings.finding: Interleaved process-driven generation substantially improves compositional and knowledge-grounded text-to-image generation over the same base model.
key_findings.evidence: On GenEval, BAGEL-7B goes from 0.77 (reproduced) to 0.83 overall, with the largest gains on Position (0.51 to 0.72) and Color Attributes (0.56 to 0.69); on WISE, 0.70 to 0.76 overall with large gains in Time (0.69 to 0.82) and Chemistry (0.58 to 0.78), matching/surpassing the 12B FLUX.1-dev.

key_findings.finding: Supervising semantically meaningful intermediate visual states is far more data- and compute-efficient than latent/noise-level process verification with search.
key_findings.evidence: The method reaches 0.83 GenEval using 62K SFT samples and 131 cumulative sampling steps (avg 2.62 reasoning steps per image), versus PARM's 0.77 with 688K samples (RL+TTS) and 1000 sampling steps from Best-of-20 search, roughly 11x less data and 8x less inference cost.

key_findings.finding: Process-level training (not external prompting) is what enables interleaved reasoning: bolting a strong external LLM onto the frozen base model fails.
key_findings.evidence: Training-free BAGEL + GPT-4o as step-by-step planner collapses to 0.60 on GenEval (vs 0.77 base), and GPT-4o as a single-round inspector gives only 0.80, both below the 0.83 of the trained model.

key_findings.finding: Critiques sampled from the model's own trajectories beat scene-graph-derived symbolic corrections, indicating supervision must lie in the model's own error distribution.
key_findings.evidence: From the multi-turn baseline (Color 0.82 / Position 0.67 / Attr 0.62), scene-graph critiques give 0.83/0.70/0.67 while self-sampled critiques give 0.87/0.72/0.69.
